subject: Limit allocations for cyber events and security addendum linkage - MSA & Order Form
messages:
From: Natalie Ross <natalie.ross@swiftcloud.com>

Cc: procurement@swiftcloud.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Initial redlines - liability caps & security addendum (MSA + OF)

Markus —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Procurement has reviewed the draft MSA and Order Form and sent over a few commercial redlines focused on liability caps and how security incidents are carved out. I attached our redline set for the MSA and a short note from legal.

High level asks from SwiftCloud:
- Remove the breach sub-limit that would place data incidents under the general liability cap (they want a separate sublimit of at least $2M)
- Explicit carve-outs for forensic costs and notification costs to be outside any cap
- No consequential damages exclusion for third-party indemnities tied to data loss

We understand Redwood has standard templates; happy to discuss a middle-ground. Our procurement team is on the thread (procurement@swiftcloud.com).

Attachments: MSA_SwiftCloud_redline.pdf, OrderForm_swift_v3.pdf

Best,
Natalie Ross
Head of Procurement — SwiftCloud Inc.
procurement@swiftcloud.com

Subject: Re: Initial redlines - liability caps & security addendum (MSA + OF)

Natalie —

Thanks for sending these — I pulled the redlines and the asks are clear. Quick internal plan:
- Legal (Rishi) to propose contract language tying a breach-specific sublimit to the security addendum rather than the general cap.
- Commercial (Laura/Karthik) to assess customer impact and propose tiered options (mid-market vs enterprise).
- Ops to provide a realistic exposure estimate based on historical incidents (we should aim to avoid open-ended limits).

My initial thinking: keep general liability cap at our standard (3x annual fees or $3M, whichever is greater), but offer a security-specific sublimit that is explicit in the security addendum. Suggested starting compromise: security sublimit = lesser of $1,000,000 or 12 months of fees; forensic/notification costs paid in addition to cap; indemnity for third-party claims preserved.

I attached a consolidated redline from our side to speed things up: MSA_redline_Markus_20260720.pdf and a draft security addendum proposing the sublimit language. Please review and tell me where SwiftCloud stands on the $1M vs $2M number.

Next step: Rishi, can you pull the exact clause language and options we can present? Laura/Karthik, please flag commercial consequences (discount/credits) if they insist on $2M+.

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Strategic Accounts

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Natalie Ross <natalie.ross@swiftcloud.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial redlines - liability caps & security addendum (MSA + OF)

Markus / team —

Read Natalie’s notes and your draft addendum. Below are recommended positions and redline text I suggest we use in the MSA + security addendum. I include two options for the sublimit so we can present a compact menu to SwiftCloud.

1) Core principles
- Keep the general liability cap (3x fees or $3M) to preserve our unit economics.
- Create a breach-specific section in the Security Addendum that: (a) defines "Security Incident"; (b) sets a defined sublimit; (c) specifies that notification and reasonable forensic costs are payable in addition to that sublimit.
- Preserve indemnity carve-outs for third-party claims arising from Customer’s data (we will accept limited carve-outs but not open-ended unlimited liability).

2) Proposed language (summary)
- "For Security Incidents, Provider’s aggregate liability shall be limited to the greater of (i) $1,000,000 and (ii) the fees paid by Customer to Provider in the twelve (12) months preceding the event. Notification, credit monitoring, and reasonable forensic investigation costs shall not be included in the calculation of the liability cap and shall be paid by Provider in addition to such cap up to a separate cap of $250,000 unless otherwise agreed in writing."

3) Two negotiation options to present to SwiftCloud:
- Option A (standard): Security sublimit = greater of $1,000,000 or 12 months fees + forensic/notification costs up to $250k outside the cap.
- Option B (premium): Security sublimit = greater of $2,000,000 or 12 months fees for enterprise deals; requires escalation to Finance for approval and triggers a 10% price uplift or committed discount forgiveness.

4) On consequential damages and indemnities
- We propose to keep a mutual consequential damages exclusion but carve back for third-party claims arising from Customer’s data breach only to the extent of direct indemnity obligations (i.e., preserve Customer’s right to recover third-party damages that are the subject of a proven indemnity claim).

Planning note: these constructions are common; the forensic cost carve-out is often a deal driver for customers. If procurement presses on $2M flat, ask for an offset (price uplift or fixed term SLA credits).

I’ll attach a short redline to the security addendum that implements Option A and the alternative language for Option B.

–Rishi
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
[attachment: security-addendum-draft.pdf]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Natalie Ross <natalie.ross@swiftcloud.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial redlines - liability caps & security addendum (MSA + OF)

Team / Natalie —

From a commercial standpoint, SwiftCloud is a key target but not yet at enterprise ARR levels. A hard $2M sublimit will push margin below acceptable thresholds for the deal size unless we get a price increase or minimum commitment. Proposed commercial counter:

- Mid-market offer (default): Option A (sublimit = greater of $1M or 12 months fees) with forensic/notification costs in addition up to $250k.
- Enterprise escalation: if SwiftCloud can commit to a 12-month minimum spend >= $750k, we move to Option B (sublimit $2M) and finalize price uplift of ~10% or an annual committed spend schedule.

Operational ask: Karthik / Ops, please confirm if our incident spend history supports the $250k forensic outside-cap assumption; if not we'll need to reduce that line.

Natalie — would the above framework be a helpful path forward or do you need a single-number position from procurement? If useful, Markus and I can hop on a short call to walk procurement through the logic and show the tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwoods Sales
[attachment: OrderForm_v3_redline.docx]

- Our consolidated MSA redline (implements breach sublimit language in the security addendum: Option A).
- Updated Order Form showing the tiered commercial path and the enterprise escalation trigger.
- Security addendum draft with explicit definitions and the forensic/notification carve-out.

Quick summary of the proposal we’d like SwiftCloud to consider:
- Keep our baseline general cap (3x fees or $3M).
- Security Incident sublimit: greater of $1,000,000 or 12 months of fees; notification and reasonable forensic costs payable in addition up to $250,000.
- If SwiftCloud can provide a 12-month committed spend >= $750k, we will consider an elevated sublimit of $2,000,000 under Option B (pricing/commitment adjustments required).

If this is acceptable in principle, can procurement confirm and we’ll circulate a DocuSign package. If not, please indicate the top 2 changes SwiftCloud needs and we’ll escalate.

Regards,
Markus
